pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The proof assumed text found in the PDF is a rule. A contents page is found in the PDF word for word.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Extends the existing not_a_control path in judge (map labels, figure captions) with one more kind; no new table, column or status.

functions.name: contents_kind
functions.input: the body text of one stored council rule, heading line removed
functions.output: 'contents_page' when 5+ lines and 3+ (40%+) end in page numbers, or 60%+ start with a dotted section number and no line has rule wording; else None
functions.if_none: an empty or None body gives no lines, so it returns None and the rule is judged as before

values.if_missing: empty body gives None, so judging continues as before

break_it.scenario: A numbers table with dotted values ('9.0 - < 11.0 | 1.1') read as a contents list.
break_it.what_happens: A real setback table would be hidden.
break_it.how: A section number must be followed by a word, not a number; test covers Woollahra B3.2.

break_it.scenario: A list of numbered controls with no page numbers.
break_it.what_happens: Real numbered rules would be hidden from visitors.
break_it.how: Any rule wording (must, shall, to be, maximum...) blocks the title-list path; test covers it.

break_it.scenario: A real contents page lists headings that contain rule words ('to be submitted').
break_it.what_happens: It would stay a rule and be proven again.
break_it.how: Three or more lines ending in page numbers decide it before rule words are checked; test uses Marrickville 2.21.
